Two hundred people put their money into a bank in Nanjing. The bank was fake.
Pukou district, twenty thirteen. It has counters, staff in bank uniforms, security guards, and LED screens with live exchange rates.
It never calls itself a bank. It says it's a cooperative.
And it pays two percent interest. Not a year. A week.
Real banks were paying about three percent a year.
Money pours in. One depositor even gets his interest paid in advance.
In about a year: almost two hundred million yuan.
Then a businessman from Hangzhou stops getting paid. After just four weeks.
He travels to Nanjing to take his money out. He can't.
He goes to the police. They find it never had a licence to take deposits.
Four people are detained. Reports say the money went into property projects that failed.
